title: Camera — one Math Engine, body, lens, tripod and a wireframe frustum
description:
A parametric CAMERA on the six-node spine — Geometry → Input Properties → Math Engine → Output Metrics → 2D Render + 3D Render.

DROP IT ON A NODE where the camera stands. Rotation aims it; the object is the viewpoint, not a picture of one.

IT DOES NOT RENDER. There is no exposure, no depth of field and no image. What it carries is where the camera is, where it looks, and the arithmetic that falls out of a focal length — which is exactly the part a plan, a shot list and a coordination drawing need, and exactly the part the renderer will not tell you until after it has run.

THE FOUR VIEW TYPES DIFFER IN TWO NUMBERS. Whether the cone converges to the eye (`_nearHW`, zero for perspective and the full half-width for orthographic) and whether the tilt survives (`_tiltDeg`, forced to zero for Two-point). Two-point is not a different camera — it is a perspective holding its verticals straight, which IS a tilt of zero, and writing it as a separate body would let the two drift.

THE FIELD OF VIEW IS ONE RIGHT TRIANGLE. `atan2(sensorWidth / 2, focalLength)` is the half-angle, and every other number here — frame width at the subject, the wedge in plan, the far rectangle in 3D — is that angle times a distance. Change the sensor and the 35 mm equivalent moves with it.

THE FRUSTUM IS A WIREFRAME, NOT A SOLID. Eight tube edges for a perspective cone, twelve for an orthographic box. A solid cone would hide the room it is pointed at, which is the one thing a camera object must never do.

THE PLAN WEDGE IS THE CONVENTIONAL SYMBOL — a triangle from the eye to the two far corners — built as a quad with two coincident points, which the kernel already accepts as a triangle. A panorama has no wedge because it has no direction, so it draws its reach as a circle instead.

DIMENSIONS AT THE DEFAULTS: a 24 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor — 73.7° horizontal, 45.9° vertical, framing 5.99 × 3.37 m at 4 m, eye at 1.372 m (4'6"), a 3 m cone.

WHAT THIS CANNOT DO. No lens distortion, no shift, no depth of field, no exposure — the renderer owns all of it. Tilt is a single axis: there is no roll. The orthographic box is framed on the subject distance rather than on a separate ortho width.

props.name: Material
props.value: matte black body, brushed aluminium lens barrel

props.name: Semantics
props.value: architectural interior camera, eye-level hero shot, verticals held straight

params.name: Camera maths
params.expr:
_natL = bodyLength
# Host frame — node, segment or space
_e1 = hcat(1, 0)
_np = rows(P)
_isSeg = _np == 2
_isSpace = _np > 2
_edges = _isSpace ? (shift(P, -1) - P) : _e1
_edgeLen = len(_edges)
_longest = max(_edgeLen)
_spaceDir = _isSpace ? row(compress(_edges, eq(_edgeLen, _longest)), 0) : _e1
_segDir = _isSeg ? (row(P, 1) - row(P, 0)) : _e1
_dir = _isSpace ? _spaceDir : (_isSeg ? _segDir : _e1)
_dirLen = len(_dir)
_axisB = _dirLen > 0 ? normalize(_dir) : _e1
_rot = rotation * PI / 180
_crot = cos(_rot)
_srot = sin(_rot)
_bx = sub(_axisB, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_by = sub(_axisB, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_axisU = hcat(_bx * _crot - _by * _srot, _bx * _srot + _by * _crot)
_axisV = (flipSide > 0 ? -1 : 1) * perp(_axisU)
_ux = sub(_axisU, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_uy = sub(_axisU, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_vx = sub(_axisV, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_vy = sub(_axisV, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_Qu = col(P, 0) * _ux + col(P, 1) * _uy
_Qv = col(P, 0) * _vx + col(P, 1) * _vy
_hu0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qu) : 0
_hu1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qu) : 0
_hv0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qv) : 0
_hv1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qv) : 0
_hcu = (_hu0 + _hu1) / 2
_hcv = (_hv0 + _hv1) / 2
_hostL = _hu1 - _hu0
_hostW = _hv1 - _hv0
# Fit to host — one uniform scale, Max never enlarges
_availL = max(0, _hostL - 2 * margin)
_notOff = fitMode != 'Off'
_exact = fitMode == 'Exact'
_sRaw = _natL > 0 ? _availL / _natL : 1
_sFit = (_notOff && _availL > 0) ? (_exact ? _sRaw : min(1, _sRaw)) : 1
scale = max(0.15, min(5, _sFit))
_s = scale
# The four view types differ in TWO numbers and nothing else: whether the cone converges to the
# eye, and whether the tilt is allowed to survive. Two-point is a perspective that holds its
# verticals straight, which IS a tilt of zero — not a different camera.
_isTwoPt = view == 'Two-point'
_isOrtho = view == 'Orthographic'
_isPano = view == 'Panorama 360'
_tiltDeg = _isTwoPt ? 0 : tilt
_tiltR = _tiltDeg * PI / 180
_eye = eyeHeight * _s
_bL = bodyLength * _s
_bW = bodyWidth * _s
_bH = bodyHeight * _s
_lensL = lensLength * _s
_lensR = lensRadius * _s
_bodyL = _bL + _lensL
_bodyW = max(_bW, tripod > 0 ? (2 * tripodSpread * _s) : _bW)
# Anchor — place the footprint by any of the nine box points
_anchorL = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Left-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left'
_anchorR = anchorDir == 'Top-Right' || anchorDir == 'Right-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_anchorT = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Top-Center' || anchorDir == 'Top-Right'
_anchorB = anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_ax = _anchorR - _anchorL
_ay = _anchorB - _anchorT
_hau = _hcu + _ax * max(0, _hostL / 2 - margin)
_hav = _hcv + _ay * max(0, _hostW / 2 - margin)
_cu = _hau - _ax * _bodyL / 2
_cv = _hav - _ay * _bodyW / 2
_wcx = _cu * _ux + _cv * _vx
_wcy = _cu * _uy + _cv * _vy
# Field of view from the focal length — the one piece of optics here, and it is a right triangle.
_halfFov = atan2(sensorWidth / 2, focalLength)
_tanH = tan(_halfFov)
_ar = aspect == '16:9' ? (16 / 9) : (aspect == '3:2' ? 1.5 : (aspect == '4:3' ? (4 / 3) : (aspect == '1:1' ? 1 : 2)))
_fL = frustumLength * _s
_dTgt = targetDistance * _s
# An orthographic cone does not converge: it is framed on the subject and stays that width the
# whole way, so the near rectangle is the far one rather than a point.
_farHW = _isOrtho ? (_dTgt * _tanH) : (_fL * _tanH)
_farHH = _farHW / _ar
_nearHW = _isOrtho ? _farHW : 0
_nearHH = _isOrtho ? _farHH : 0
_farZ = _eye + _fL * tan(_tiltR)
# Body and lens. The body sits BEHIND the eye point, so the lens leaves from the origin and the
# frustum starts there too — otherwise the drawn cone and the drawn camera disagree by a body.
_BODY = hcat(0 - _bL, 0 - _bW / 2, 0, 0 - _bW / 2, 0, _bW / 2, 0 - _bL, _bW / 2, _eye - _bH / 2, _eye + _bH / 2, 1)
Q = _BODY
# Quad prism — every part is a quad swept from z0 to z1 (6 faces)
_nq = rows(Q)
_r4 = ones(4,1)
_a1 = col(Q,0)
_b1 = col(Q,1)
_a2 = col(Q,2)
_b2 = col(Q,3)
_a3 = col(Q,4)
_b3 = col(Q,5)
_a4 = col(Q,6)
_b4 = col(Q,7)
_qz0 = col(Q,8)
_qz1 = col(Q,9)
_gq = kron(col(Q,10), _r4)
_fq = kron(arange(_nq), _r4) * 6
_q0 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 0, _gq)
_q1 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 1, _gq)
_q2 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a1,_b1,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 2, _gq)
_q3 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 3, _gq)
_q4 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 4, _gq)
_q5 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 5, _gq)
_FL = vcat(_q0,_q1,_q2,_q3,_q4,_q5)
_PL = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_a2,_b2,_a3,_b3,_a4,_b4), 4*_nq, 2), kron(arange(_nq), _r4), _gq)
# Local (u,v,z) -> world, once, for every part at the same time
_U = _cu + col(_FL,0)
_V = _cv + col(_FL,1)
_W = hcat(_U * _ux + _V * _vx, _U * _uy + _V * _vy, col(_FL,2), col(_FL,3), col(_FL,4))
_nw = rows(_W)
_PU = _cu + col(_PL,0)
_PV = _cv + col(_PL,1)
_WP = hcat(_PU * _ux + _PV * _vx, _PU * _uy + _PV * _vy, col(_PL,2), col(_PL,3))
_nwp = rows(_WP)
Body3D = sub(compress(_W, eq(col(_W,4), 1)), 0, 0, _nw, 4)
BodyPlan = sub(compress(_WP, eq(col(_WP,3), 1)), 0, 0, _nwp, 3)
# Lens — a cylinder leaving the eye point along the tilted view axis.
_lensEndU = _lensL * cos(_tiltR)
_lensEndZ = _eye + _lensL * sin(_tiltR)
_LENS = hcat(0, 0, _eye, _lensEndU, 0, _lensEndZ, _lensR)
_t1u = _cu + col(_LENS,0)
_t1v = _cv + col(_LENS,1)
_t2u = _cu + col(_LENS,3)
_t2v = _cv + col(_LENS,4)
Lens3D = hcat(_t1u * _ux + _t1v * _vx, _t1u * _uy + _t1v * _vy, col(_LENS,2), _t2u * _ux + _t2v * _vx, _t2u * _uy + _t2v * _vy, col(_LENS,5), col(_LENS,6))
# Tripod — three legs from under the body to the floor, splayed on a circle.
_legK = arange(3)
_legA = _legK * 2 * PI / 3 + PI
_spread = tripodSpread * _s
_legZ = _eye - _bH / 2
_legR = 0.012 * _s
_LEGr = hcat(fill(3,1,0), fill(3,1,0), fill(3,1,_legZ), _spread * cos(_legA), _spread * sin(_legA), fill(3,1,0), fill(3,1,_legR))
_LEGS = tripod > 0 ? _LEGr : zeros(0, 7)
_t1u = _cu + col(_LEGS,0)
_t1v = _cv + col(_LEGS,1)
_t2u = _cu + col(_LEGS,3)
_t2v = _cv + col(_LEGS,4)
Tripod3D = hcat(_t1u * _ux + _t1v * _vx, _t1u * _uy + _t1v * _vy, col(_LEGS,2), _t2u * _ux + _t2v * _vx, _t2u * _uy + _t2v * _vy, col(_LEGS,5), col(_LEGS,6))
# The frustum is a WIREFRAME, not a solid — eight edges for a perspective cone, twelve for an
# orthographic box. A solid cone would hide the room it is pointed at, which is the one thing a
# camera object must never do.
_eR = edgeRadius * _s
_f1u = _fL
_fzLo = _farZ - _farHH
_fzHi = _farZ + _farHH
_nzLo = _eye - _nearHH
_nzHi = _eye + _nearHH
_R1 = hcat(0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzLo, _f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzLo, _eR)
_R2 = hcat(0, _nearHW, _nzLo, _f1u, _farHW, _fzLo, _eR)
_R3 = hcat(0, _nearHW, _nzHi, _f1u, _farHW, _fzHi, _eR)
_R4 = hcat(0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzHi, _f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzHi, _eR)
_F1 = hcat(_f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzLo, _f1u, _farHW, _fzLo, _eR)
_F2 = hcat(_f1u, _farHW, _fzLo, _f1u, _farHW, _fzHi, _eR)
_F3 = hcat(_f1u, _farHW, _fzHi, _f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzHi, _eR)
_F4 = hcat(_f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzHi, _f1u, 0 - _farHW, _fzLo, _eR)
_N1 = hcat(0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzLo, 0, _nearHW, _nzLo, _eR)
_N2 = hcat(0, _nearHW, _nzLo, 0, _nearHW, _nzHi, _eR)
_N3 = hcat(0, _nearHW, _nzHi, 0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzHi, _eR)
_N4 = hcat(0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzHi, 0, 0 - _nearHW, _nzLo, _eR)
_RAYS = vcat(_R1, _R2, _R3, _R4, _F1, _F2, _F3, _F4)
_NEAR = _isOrtho ? vcat(_N1, _N2, _N3, _N4) : zeros(0, 7)
_FRUSTr = vcat(_RAYS, _NEAR)
_FRUST = (showFrustum > 0 && _isPano == 0) ? _FRUSTr : zeros(0, 7)
_t1u = _cu + col(_FRUST,0)
_t1v = _cv + col(_FRUST,1)
_t2u = _cu + col(_FRUST,3)
_t2v = _cv + col(_FRUST,4)
Frustum3D = hcat(_t1u * _ux + _t1v * _vx, _t1u * _uy + _t1v * _vy, col(_FRUST,2), _t2u * _ux + _t2v * _vx, _t2u * _uy + _t2v * _vy, col(_FRUST,5), col(_FRUST,6))
# Plan symbols. The wedge is the conventional camera symbol — a triangle from the eye to the two
# far corners — built as a quad with two coincident points, which the kernel already accepts.
_wU = _cu
_wV = _cv
_pe = hcat(_wcx, _wcy)
_pLu = _wU + _f1u
_pLv = _wV - _farHW
_pRv = _wV + _farHW
_wx1 = _wU * _ux + _wV * _vx
_wy1 = _wU * _uy + _wV * _vy
_wx2 = _pLu * _ux + _pLv * _vx
_wy2 = _pLu * _uy + _pLv * _vy
_wx3 = _pLu * _ux + _pRv * _vx
_wy3 = _pLu * _uy + _pRv * _vy
_WEDGEr = vcat(hcat(_wx1, _wy1, 1), hcat(_wx2, _wy2, 1), hcat(_wx3, _wy3, 1))
WedgePlan = (showFrustum > 0 && _isPano == 0) ? _WEDGEr : zeros(0, 3)
PanoPlan = _isPano ? hcat(_wcx, _wcy, _fL) : zeros(0, 3)
EyePlan = hcat(_wcx, _wcy, max(_lensR, 0.04 * _s))
# Metrics — everything a shot list needs, and nothing the renderer owns.
horizontalFov = 2 * _halfFov * 180 / PI
verticalFov = 2 * atan2(_tanH / _ar, 1) * 180 / PI
frameWidth = 2 * _dTgt * _tanH
frameHeight = frameWidth / _ar
eyeLevel = _eye
tiltUsed = _tiltDeg
aspectRatio = _ar
focal35mm = focalLength * 36 / sensorWidth
coneLength = _fL
subjectDistance = _dTgt
isPanorama = _isPano ? 1 : 0
isOrthographic = _isOrtho ? 1 : 0
footprintRadius = _isPano ? _fL : _farHW
